NC500 in 7 Days: The Definitive Motorcycle Experience

Seven days on the NC500 transforms a road trip into an immersive Highland experience. With daily distances averaging just 75 miles, you have time for detours, walking, wildlife spotting, and genuinely connecting with the landscape. This is how the NC500 was meant to be ridden.

Day 1: Inverness to Dornoch (65 miles)

A gentle start along the Moray Firth. Stop at the Black Isle to spot bottlenose dolphins from Chanonry Point. Cross the Cromarty Firth and settle into Dornoch — a beautiful small town with a medieval cathedral and championship golf course. Short day, maximum relaxation.

Day 2: Dornoch to Wick (70 miles)

Continue north along the coast. Dunrobin Castle deserves a proper visit — the falconry display is remarkable. The Caithness coastline beyond Helmsdale is rugged and impressive. Wick has genuine character as a former herring port.

Day 3: Wick to Tongue (80 miles)

Round the top of Britain via John o' Groats and Dunnet Head (the actual most northerly point of mainland Britain — John o' Groats isn't). The Castle of Mey, former home of the Queen Mother, is worth a stop. The road west to Tongue passes through increasingly wild country.

Day 4: Tongue to Kylesku (75 miles)

This section along the A838 through the far northwest is Scotland at its most remote. Loch Eriboll is vast and lonely. Beyond Durness, the landscape becomes almost Scandinavian — bare rock, isolated lochs, and enormous skies. Kylesku Bridge is a stunning place to end the day.

By day 4, the NC500 has you completely. The pace of life slows, the phone signal disappears, and you remember why you started riding in the first place.

Day 5: Kylesku to Ullapool (60 miles)

The shortest day but possibly the most beautiful. The road through Lochinver and Inverpolly passes Suilven, Cul Mor, and Stac Pollaidh — extraordinary mountains rising from a primordial landscape. Ullapool is a perfect rest stop with great seafood restaurants and a vibrant music scene.

Day 6: Ullapool to Applecross (85 miles)

Head south to tackle the Bealach na Bà. Seven days in, you've been building to this moment — and it doesn't disappoint. Britain's greatest pass, with hairpin bends, vertigo-inducing drops, and views to Skye. Applecross Inn is the perfect celebration point with local prawns and cold beer.

Day 7: Applecross to Inverness (100 miles)

The coast road from Applecross to Shieldaig is single-track magic. Through Torridon and Glen Carron, the mountains gradually soften as you approach Inverness. A bittersweet final day — the NC500 doesn't want to let you go.

7-Day Extras

With seven days, you can also include: a boat trip to Handa Island (seabird colony near Scourie), the Bone Caves near Inchnadamph, Corrieshalloch Gorge near Ullapool, and the Inverewe Gardens. keyTakeaways: Seven days averages just 75 miles a day, turning a road trip into an immersive Highland experience.
Day 1 is a gentle 65 miles to Dornoch, with dolphin spotting from Chanonry Point on the Black Isle.
Day 3 rounds the top of Britain via John o' Groats and Dunnet Head, the true most northerly point.
Day 6 saves the Bealach na Ba for a well-earned climax before Applecross Inn.
Spare time allows extras such as a boat trip to Handa Island, the Bone Caves and Corrieshalloch Gorge.

faq.q: What does the extra time on a 7-day NC500 give you?
faq.a: With daily distances averaging just 75 miles, you gain time for detours, walking, wildlife spotting and genuinely connecting with the landscape. Extras include a boat trip to Handa Island near Scourie, the Bone Caves near Inchnadamph, Corrieshalloch Gorge near Ullapool and Inverewe Gardens.

faq.q: What is the true most northerly point of mainland Britain?
faq.a: Dunnet Head, not John o' Groats, is the actual most northerly point of mainland Britain, reached on day three between Wick and Tongue. The Castle of Mey, former home of the Queen Mother, is worth a stop along this rugged Caithness coastline.

faq.q: Which day is the most beautiful on the 7-day route?
faq.a: Day five from Kylesku to Ullapool is the shortest at 60 miles but possibly the most beautiful, passing Suilven, Cul Mor and Stac Pollaidh rising from a primordial landscape near Lochinver and Inverpolly. Ullapool makes a superb rest stop with seafood and a vibrant music scene.

faq.q: Is the Bealach na Ba worth saving for later in the week?
faq.a: Yes. On the seven-day plan you tackle it on day six, having built up to the moment, and it does not disappoint. Britain's greatest pass delivers hairpin bends, vertigo-inducing drops and views to Skye, with the Applecross Inn the perfect celebration point afterwards.
